paper_metadata.title: An 8-bit 80-Msample/s Pipelined Analog-to-Digital Converter With Background Calibration
paper_metadata.abstract: An 8-bit 80-Msample/s pipelined analog-to-digital converter (ADC) uses monolithic background calibration to reduce the nonlinearity caused by interstage gain errors. Test results show that the ADC achieves a peak signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio of 43.8 dB, a peak integral nonlinearity of 0.51 least significant bit (LSB), and a peak differential nonlinearity of 0.32 LSB with active background calibration. It dissipates 268 mW from a 3-V supply and occupies 10.3 mm2 in a single-poly 0.5m CMOS technology.

sections.title: CONCLUSION
sections.text_preview: This paper shows that applying background calibration to the design of pipelined ADCs is of potential interest to overcome the ADC nonlinearity that would otherwise result from interstage gain errors. This technique can be extended to more stages and higher resolution as long as the dominant source of nonlinearity stems from interstage gain error.
